cards.text: Jacob's on his way home, and word comes that his brother Esau is coming to meet him with four hundred men. Jacob is in great fear and distress. He sends herd after herd of gifts ahead of him and spends the night in camp.
During the night, Jacob gets up and takes his two wives, his two maidservants and his eleven sons across the ford of the Jabbok. He sends them over the stream with everything he owns.

cards.question: With his family across the Jabbok, Jacob keeps a few servants with him for the night.

cards.text: So Jacob is left all alone, and there a man wrestles with him until daybreak. I spent YEARS in the dark in a junk drawer, friend, and the roughest thing that ever jumped me was a rubber band.

cards.question: Jacob and the man wrestle all night long. What does the man see as they wrestle?

answers.text: Jacob is ready to give up
Jacob is too tired to fight

cards.question: When the man sees he can't overpower Jacob, he strikes the socket of Jacob's ___.

cards.text: Jacob's hip is dislocated, and the man says, “Let me go, for it is daybreak.” If MY hip popped out I'd let go of EVERYTHING, friend, but Jacob says he won't let go unless the man blesses him.
The man asks Jacob his name, then says his name will no longer be Jacob. Most folks need a stack of forms and a LONG line to change their name, friend, and Jacob gets it done mid-wrestle.

cards.question: What new name does the man give Jacob?
Why the name Israel, according to the man who wrestled Jacob?

answers.text: Jacob has struggled with God and with men and prevailed
Jacob has run from God and from men and escaped
Jacob has pleased God and men and been honored

cards.text: Now Jacob asks, “Please tell me your name.” Fair enough, friend, because if you wrestle somebody ALL NIGHT, you want to know who it is.

cards.question: Instead of giving his name, the man asks, “Why do you ask my name?” Then he ___ Jacob there.
Jacob names the place Peniel. What reason does he give?

answers.text: He has seen God face to face and his life was spared
He has won the hardest fight of his whole life
He has finally made peace with his brother Esau

cards.text: The sun rises above Jacob as he passes by Penuel. Friend, Jacob went into that night in great fear of his brother and comes out of it with a NEW NAME.

cards.question: How is Jacob getting around as the sun rises over him?

answers.text: Riding on one of his camels

cards.question: To this day the Israelites don't eat the tendon attached to the socket of the hip. Why not?

answers.text: Jacob's hip was struck near that tendon
That tendon was set aside for the priests
That tendon was kept for their offerings

cards.text: Hang on to your apron, friend. Jacob's story keeps going, and I'm not saying another WORD about it yet.

findings.problem: The blank asks for a body part that has not been mentioned or made inferable by any earlier card. Both "hip" and "shoulder" fit a socket, so the baker has to guess an unseen detail rather than reason out the meaning.

rule.text: The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The card cites only Genesis 32:31, but its second sentence also retells Jacob's fear from Genesis 32:7 and his new name from Genesis 32:28. The citation does not run from the first verse the card uses to the last.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.
